c_stagmor.text: The stag lifts a head like a coat rack and considers you. You are not a threat. You are barely a footnote.

c_fawnlet.text: It trots three paces, stops, stares, and trots back. Calves are professionals at looking lost.

c_kerryspot.text: A big dark slug with pale spots. It's the Kerry slug, found in Kerry and Spain and practically nowhere else. It is not in a hurry.

jarvey.text: Jaunting cars have carried visitors round Killarney for two hundred years. I'm a jarvey. The horse is the boss, I just hold the reins.
Don't be hearing 'it's a tourist thing'. It's a very old tourist thing. Fáilte, anyway.

then.text: Five. Of course it was five. That's what I wrote in the book. I'd been counting them as six, on account of one's very round.
The rut is in a fortnight. Bring earplugs and a flask. The stags sound like a very large cow with a tragic secret.

else.text: Killarney is home to Ireland's only native herd of red deer. They've been here since the last Ice Age, and survived hunting, wolves and tourists.

then.text: How many red deer have you counted around the lakes?
Five! Two stags and three fawns! That's exactly what I have in the book. Go raibh maith agat, as we say. That's 'thank you'. Here, for your trouble.

else.text: Hmm. That's not what the book says. Have another wander, and count the ones in the open and by the water. The shy ones count too.
I count them every autumn at the rut. The stags roar. It sounds like a very large cow with a tragic secret.
I'm one short in my sums this year. Would you count them for me? Stags and fawns on this stretch only. Walk the lakes, then come back and tell me.

lake_painter.text: Cill Airne, the Irish name for Killarney, means the church of the sloes. That's the blackthorn berry. It's the colour I can't ever get right.
I've done the same lake eleven times. Every time the weather has moved it. Every time I'm not wrong.

kerry_farmer.text: Kerry Bog Ponies are small, hardy and not at all impressed by you. And the Kerry cow is one of the oldest breeds in Europe.
Hang on. Is that a slug? That's the Kerry slug. It's more famous than the cow, these days. The cow has taken it badly.

reeks_walker.text: Carrauntoohil in the Reeks is Ireland's highest. It's 1,038 metres and it will tell you every one of them.
My advice: start at dawn, take a waterproof, and never trust a path that's called the Devil's Ladder.
